semanticChecks: Validate source bundle, entry point, dependency lock and runtime raw-byte digests; execute candidate code only in the declared host isolation boundary, never inside Core.
The host must enforce process isolation, read-only declared inventory, finite resource limits and the exact grant ceiling; unavailable required capability blocks preparation and native dispatch.

Bind the prompt bytes and ordered context references to the exact approved work item, configuration, project overview and preparation inputs; validate ranks and inventories without adding hidden context.
Preparation code cannot dispatch agents, modify evaluation tests, grant capabilities, select Core routes, waive reviews, activate harnesses or write authoritative ProjectMemory.
Validate budget accounting units and actual observations; unknown resource accounting is explicit and cannot satisfy a comparison policy that requires measurement.

Finalize and persist the PreparedWorkerRequest bytes first, then checkpoint that request and preparation observations, then finalize the successful PreparationReceipt with the exact request raw-byte digest. The receipt must match the request input and harness, and its source/runtime identity must match the pinned harness. Persist the receipt before constructing NativeExecutionInput, which binds both artifacts. No referenced earlier checkpoint may depend on the subsequent receipt digest.

schema.title: MES-001 DESKTOP interface
schema.description: Bounded native Desktop execution evidence with existing task-plan and ownership references. Native completion grants no lifecycle approval.

preparationReceipt.description: Successful PreparationReceipt finalized after preparedRequest; the host resolves and verifies their exact binding before dispatch.

checkpoint.description: Earlier durable checkpoint of the execution history and worker/review/repair evidence. Final result persistence precedes the subsequent verification handoff; this checkpoint cannot depend on that handoff or on the containing result digest.

BoundedExecutionResult.description: Finalize this execution candidate before independent verification creates a VerificationCandidateHandoff referring to its exact bytes. The result cannot reference the later handoff.

semanticChecks: Core alone derives ready work; validate the existing DesktopTaskPlan, bootstrap/memory context, quality resolution, reuse decision, exact starting revision, grants and prompt before dispatch.
The durable lease/claim owner validates current expiry, fencing token and ownership at prepare, dispatch and commit using the owning clock; stale owners cannot dispatch, commit or release successors.
Bind each native request, task identity, raw permitted reply and checkpoint to the exact attempt and dispatch key; repeated delivery reuses only a revalidated durable receipt.
Ambiguous native dispatch remains blocked until the existing host reconciliation owner proves the effect or authorizes recovery; a missing response is never permission to retry.
Validate ordered worker/review/repair lineage and independent reviewer assignment, subject digest and distinct native task evidence; reject self-review or review of stale source bytes.
Zeroshot internal scheduling cannot release Core dependency frontiers or perform ChangeIntegration; terminal execution remains a candidate for WorkItemVerification and existing Gates.
Validate engine source and graph configuration digests, supported native settings and capability evidence; fixture model identities and inheritance markers do not attest an actual model.

Before dispatch, resolve the successful PreparationReceipt and PreparedWorkerRequest from NativeExecutionInput and validate their exact raw-byte digest, input, harness, configuration and source/runtime bindings. The prepared request must not refer back to the subsequent receipt.

Persist worker/review/repair artifacts and their history checkpoint before finalizing BoundedExecutionResult. Persist the exact result before independent verification and its subsequent handoff; never require a result digest and its later verification-handoff digest to embed one another. Earlier checkpoints must not depend on the containing later result.

schema.title: MES-001 QUALITY interface
schema.description: References existing quality, work-continuity and project-control artifacts at their owning boundaries; introduces no duplicate policy or reuse authority.

boundedExecutionResult.description: Exact finalized BoundedExecutionResult persisted before this handoff; the result contains no verification-handoff backlink.

semanticChecks: Resolve quality policy, QualityObligationResolution, WorkFingerprint, WorkReuseDecision, continuity index and project-control artifacts through their existing owning schemas and validators.
The owning quality runtime validates the approved policy version, exact work identity, current obligations and all independent verification evidence; this envelope cannot weaken those obligations.
Reuse requires exact fingerprint and source/evidence equality plus a valid durable completion checkpoint; similarity, prior success or missing evidence cannot authorize reuse.
Validate continuity-index freshness and durable ownership before dispatch; stale or conflicting work routes through existing project-control reconciliation.
Verification candidates remain candidate-only until the existing owning Gate validates and approves them; neither a provider authority label nor this schema establishes approval.
Checkpoint the exact owning resolution and evidence before preparation; on restart revalidate the same result without promoting cloned or stale authority.

Resolve and verify the exact finalized BoundedExecutionResult before producing independent verification receipts, the owning verification candidate and Gate request, then finalize VerificationCandidateHandoff referencing those earlier artifacts. Reject stale result bytes and handoff backlinks; the handoff itself grants no verification or approval authority.

semanticChecks: Resolve the preregistered comparison policy before any evaluation and verify minimum successes, gain, repetitions, noise handling and non-regression rules; this contract does not author activation approval policy.
Verify frozen source/dependency/runtime bytes and checkpoint precede all held-out episodes, and reject changed evaluator/test bytes, partition leakage or held-out feedback into search.

Compare baseline A, baseline B and candidate on the same sealed episode set and repetitions with attested equal actual solver identity, model settings, tools, grants, runtime and limits; require exactly one identity per role.
Validate the full trial and episode ledger including failures, invalid, timed-out, unavailable and interrupted runs; omitted episodes and missing raw receipts produce incomplete evidence.
Verify independent acceptance, authority and regression observations for each episode. Quality or authority failures cannot be offset by faster runtime, lower cost or other secondary gains.
Derive every metric and summary from permitted raw observations with correct units; unknown values remain unknown, and missing policy-required accounting blocks qualification.

Only the owning evaluator can establish comparable qualification by validating model attestation provenance, matched identities and policy evidence; fixture-only model identity and Desktop inheritance cannot establish live improvement.
A qualified candidate still requires exact owning approval for activation. Report no-improvement, incomparable or incomplete when their evidence warrants it, including finite-sample limitations.
Validate resource budget consumption and exact effect checkpoints across restart; ambiguous native dispatch must be reconciled without duplicate execution.

schema.title: MES-001 ACTIVATION interface
schema.description: Owner-reviewed immutable harness selection and explicit rollback for future runs only. Approval evidence must be authenticated by its existing owning Gate.

semanticChecks: Resolve the exact qualification candidate/report, immutable harness source and comparison policy; verify the owning evaluator established qualified status using authentic model and required accounting evidence.

The existing owning Gate must authenticate explicit owner intent, approval decision, Gate receipt and exact policy version; provider-supplied strings or syntactically valid references do not prove approval.
Owner review remains the conservative approved assumption while the automatic-activation question is unanswered; no optimizer, proposer, executor or evaluator may self-activate.
Validate that approval subject, target harness digest, experiment, qualification, evaluation report and policy all identify the same immutable candidate.
Compare the expected current activation against the durable head atomically, checkpoint the exact activation receipt and preserve all prior versions; stale requests cannot mutate state.
Rollback requires a prior immutable approved activation and its authentic owning approval plus explicit current rollback authorization; it cannot bypass qualification or select arbitrary source.
Activation and rollback affect subsequent new runs only; verify existing active runs retain their original configuration and harness bindings.
Validate idempotency and receipt replay through the existing activation owner; duplicate requests do not create another activation version.

schema.title: MES-001 TRACE interface
schema.description: Trusted projection envelopes around existing graph-owner artifacts. No adapter receives graph service, graph mutation authority or approval authority.

semanticChecks: Only Core may invoke a registered version-pinned trusted contributor with graph context; authenticate registration and invocation evidence rather than trusting supplied authority labels.
Resolve canonical source bytes, Core execution receipts and validation receipts before projection; approved sources additionally require exact authentic owning Gate approval and promotion receipts.
The contributor registration must authorize each declared node/edge kind and candidate or approved scope; validate current graph vocabulary and reject cross-owner or cross-scope assertions.
Adapters never receive the graph service or submit graph operations. Contributors derive assertions only from validated source artifacts and cannot create new approval facts.
Persist the exact prepared update checkpoint before merge, then verify the graph application receipt and resulting checkpoint against those stored bytes.
Exact replay reuses the stored prepared update and receipt without rerunning an adapter or contributor; reject mismatched invocation, source, checkpoint or result graph.
Candidate and approved observations remain distinct authority identities; retire or supersede graph history without deleting prior observations.
Missing contributors, validation, approval or ownership proof fail closed for evidence-bearing results; expose horizon diagnostics without bypassing Core progression.
